sentences.text:
This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:

Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice H.T. Narendra Prasad
 Oral Judgment
1.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act', for short) has been filed by the Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award dated 28.10.2019 passed by the MACT, Bengaluru in MVC No.118/2018.
2.

Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 24.06.2017 at about 5.00 p.m., the NC: 2024:KHC:37402 deceased N.Vyshnavi was traveling towards Bengaluru side as a pillion rider in offending motor bike bearing Registration No.KA-05-JQ-1628 ridden by its rider from Yadiyur side, while so traveling near U-turn at Urkalli Village, the rider of the said Bike was riding the same in very high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the name board wall of Shanidevara Temple and caused accident.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
3. The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of the deceased along with interest.

sentences.text: Upon service of notice, the respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared through counsel and filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.

On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.

The Tribunal, by impugned judgment and award has partly allowed the claim petition and held that the claimants are entitled to a compensation of Rs.29,34,120/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, this appeal has been filed.

6. The learned counsel for the Insurance Company has raised the following counter-contentions:
a) Firstly, the evidence presented by the parties indicates that the accident occurred due to negligence of the motorcycle rider.
Notably, at the time of the accident, the deceased was not wearing a helmet.
According to the post-mortem report, the cause of death was head injuries.

Despite this, the Tribunal erred in holding the motorcycle rider solely responsible for the accident,
failing to NC: 2024:KHC:37402 recognize the deceased's contributory negligence in traveling on a two-wheeler without wearing a helmet.
b) Secondly, although the claimants alleged that the deceased was working in a private company and earning Rs.19,208/- per month, as per the Salary Certificates (Ex.P15), the Tribunal, after considering the evidence, assessed the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.19,208/-, which seems to be on the higher side.
Even they have not produced the Bank Statement to prove that she was earning Rs.19,208/- per month.
With the above contentions, the learned counsel sought to allow the appeal.

7. The learned counsel for the claimants has raised the following contentions:
a) Firstly, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the motorcycle rider.

Although the deceased was not wearing a helmet, which is an offense under the Act,
but it did not contribute to the accident.

Therefore, the Tribunal NC:
2024:KHC:37402 has rightly held that the deceased did not contribute to the accident.
b) Secondly, considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
With the above contentions, the learned counsel sought to dismissal of the appeal.

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
REG:NEGLIGENCE:
9. The specific case of PW-1 is that the deceased was traveling as a pillion rider on a motorcycle.
The accident occurred due to the negligence of the motorcycle rider.
The Tribunal has also made a clear finding that the accident was caused by the rider's negligence.

Merely because the deceased was a pillion rider and not wearing a helmet, it cannot be inferred that they contributed to the accident unless it is proved that not wearing a helmet was NC: 2024:KHC:37402 a violation of the Act.
Although not wearing a helmet is an offense under the Act, it cannot be assumed that the deceased contributed to the accident.
Therefore, the Insurance company's contention that the deceased was also responsible for the accident cannot be accepted.

REG: QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION:
10.
The claimants claim that deceased was working a Associate in W.N.S. Global Service Pvt. Ltd.
They produced Salary Certificate as per Ex.P15 and they also examined the employer of the deceased as PW-2.
Based on these evidences, the Tribunal has made a reasonable assessment of the deceased's monthly income.
Therefore, the contention of the appellant cannot be accepted.
The appellant has not made out any case to interfere with the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

11. Accordingly, the following order is passed:
ORDER a) The appeal is dismissed.
NC: 2024:KHC:37402 b) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is confirmed.
c) The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal.

Sd/-
(H.T. NARENDRA PRASAD) JUDGE HA
